Key Features of the Nvidia Vera Rubin Architecture

At the GTC 2026 event, Nvidia unveiled Vera Rubin, its next-generation computing platform consisting of seven different chips. Designed to replace Blackwell systems, the platform delivers up to 10 times higher inference efficiency per watt while reducing the processing cost per token by a factor of ten.

According to Nvidia’s data, the new architecture can perform the same task with just one-fourth the number of GPUs required by Blackwell systems to train large mixed-expert (MoE) models. The infrastructure is supported by major cloud providers such as Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud, Microsoft Azure, and Oracle Cloud, as well as AI developers like OpenAI, Anthropic, and Meta.

A Seven-Rack Unified Supercomputer Architecture

Optimized specifically for agentic (autonomous agent) AI systems and reinforcement learning, Vera Rubin consists of five different rack-scale systems that operate like a unified supercomputer. The system’s hardware infrastructure includes the following core components:

  • NVL72 Rack: Combines 72 Rubin GPUs and 36 Vera CPUs into a single unit, with the components communicating via NVLink 6 switches.
  • Vera CPU Rack: It houses 256 liquid-cooled processors capable of supporting more than 22,500 concurrent environments. The processors operate with LPDDR5X memory offering 1.2 terabytes per second of bandwidth and 88 custom-designed Olympus cores.
  • Groq 3 LPX Rack: Integrates 256 custom inference processors with 128 GB of on-chip SRAM to meet the low-latency demands of trillion-parameter models.
  • Network and Storage (BlueField-4 STX / Spectrum-6 SPX): The BlueField-4 DPU provides high-speed storage for the massive key-value caches generated by agentic systems, while the Spectrum-6 delivers five times higher optical power efficiency compared to traditional hardware.

The Vera Rubin platform is scheduled to be made generally available in the second half of 2026 through leading cloud service providers and hardware manufacturers.
